keystone_added.concept: Logical query processing order: FROM -> WHERE -> GROUP BY -> HAVING -> SELECT -> WINDOW -> DISTINCT -> ORDER BY -> LIMIT
keystone_added.why: Was absent from the entire plan. It is the root cause of three separate traps already present (alias-in-WHERE, aggregate-in-WHERE, window-in-HAVING), and its absence had produced an outright factual error in the Day 9 business-case hints.

errors_corrected: HARD TECHNICAL ERROR (Day 9): 'window function for rolling avg, then HAVING' — impossible; window functions evaluate AFTER HAVING. Replaced with the correct CTE + outer WHERE pattern plus worked SQL.
Day 7: 'Index Seek' listed as a PostgreSQL EXPLAIN node — that is SQL Server terminology. Replaced with the real Postgres node types (Seq Scan, Index Scan, Index Only Scan, Bitmap Index/Heap Scan).
Day 7: 'Seq Scan = usually bad' — wrong and a junior tell; seq scan is optimal above ~5-10% selectivity. Corrected with the interview line.
Day 7: 'Index Scan: O(log n)' -> O(log n + k).
Day 7: clustered-index content taught without noting PostgreSQL HAS NO clustered indexes — while the whole plan practises in PostgreSQL. Dialect boundary now explicit.
Day 4: SQL Server temp-table syntax (#tmp/##tmp/@tbl) presented unlabelled in a PostgreSQL plan. Labelled.
Day 6: isolation-level table presented as universal — it is the ANSI standard; Postgres RR and InnoDB RR both block phantoms. Caveat added.
Day 6: UNIQUE + NULL behaviour is dialect-split (SQL Server one NULL, Postgres/Oracle many). Noted.
ARITHMETIC: Day 4 header said 5.5h, blocks summed to 4.75h. Day 6 header said 5.5h, blocks summed to 6.25h. Both corrected and all 10 days re-verified.

adaptive_engine.principle: Self-healing control loop: SENSE (daily log) -> COMPARE (plan vs actual) -> DIAGNOSE (RAG) -> ADAPT (re-plan) -> ROLLOVER at 30-day boundary. Plan bends to reality; hours fixed, content flexes.

study_budget.assumption: REVISED 2026-07-24: high leeway — very light work, mostly WFH. Time is NOT the constraint; cognition + spacing are.
study_budget.session_distribution: 3 distributed blocks/day (morning intake ~2h, midday practice ~2h, evening retrieval+review ~1.5-2h). Distributed practice > massed — spacing across the day is itself a retention multiplier.
study_budget.key_constraint_insight: Extra hours go to MORE distributed practice + retrieval reps + mocks, NOT more new-concept cramming (quality ceiling ~4h/day intake, Ericsson). Critically: SM2 spacing has a CALENDAR FLOOR — you cannot review something at +7d in 3 days no matter the hours. So calendar stays ~30 days; extra hours buy DEPTH + EARLIER READINESS + bigger buffer, not a shorter cycle.
study_budget.strategic_consequence: Intake finishes early -> later cycle days become mock/practice-heavy -> readiness gauge climbs sooner (interview-viable ~day 18-22, days 22-30 = deep practice + buffer). Ideal hedge for KPIT-fast uncertainty.
